newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 29.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 29.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

WASHINGTON - The U.S. government charges that R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co.'s "Joe Camel" cartoon ads illegally promote its "addictive and dangerous" cigarettes to children and adolescents. The Federal Trade Commission votes 3-2 to bring the cigarette maker before an administrative law judge, demanding the company cease targeting children under 18.

LONDON - Forget about drinking milk because your mother told you it was good for you. The European Commission is to run a $10 million ad campaign to persuade young people to drink it because it's "modern" and nutritious.

NEW YORK - Preston Padden, the new president of Walt Disney Co's ABC television network, says he is "optimistic" about the early advertising market after the network unveiled its fall schedule last week.

MELBOURNE - Australia's Victoria state announces it will back local car makers with a major advertising campaign arguing against proposed cuts to tariffs on imported cars. Victoria's ad campaign will be run nationally and argue for a freeze on tariffs at 15 percent until at least 2005.
NEW YORK - Edelman Public Relations says it is reorganising its New York office into three operating units, one of which is a new division, Edelman Financial Worldwide.
LONDON - British market research company Taylor Nelson AGB Plc says it has bought leading Danish media research company Gallup A/S for an initial 4.8 million pounds ($7.9 million).
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LOS ANGELES - Canadian beverage and entertainment giant Seagram Co. Ltd. sells nearly half its stake in Time Warner Inc. for $1.39 billion in cash. Seagram, the third largest shareholder in Time Warner, has long been considering a sale of its Time Warner holdings.
MADRID - Spanish Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado says Spain will push terrestrial digital television.

SYDNEY - John Fairfax Holdings Ltd chairman Sir Laurence Street says any government proposal leading to the break-up of the Fairfax newspaper group would be against Australia's national interest. The company is Australia's oldest newspaper publisher.
NEW YORK - Television is the number one source of news for most Americans, far outpacing newspapers and radio, according to a network-sponsored poll.
MILAN - An Italian prison launches an internet site which allows inmates virtual access to the outside world. Inmates will be able to surf the net but access will be limited.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LOS ANGELES - The $40 billion record industry is cutting back on music videos, which are in oversupply, as sales and radio airplay determine the few select videos that get broadcast. Employees at the big six music labels say the current video glut is due, in part, to a shift at Viacom Inc.'s MTV channel away from all-music programming.

TOKYO - Mitsubishi Motors Corp says it expects its combined domestic vehicle sales and exports in the year from April 1, 1997, to be 1.34 million units, up from its combined domestic sales and exports of 1.25 million units in the previous year.

BRUSSELS - Retailers join forces to urge the European Union to scrap rules allowing banks to impose "excessive" charges on shops and restaurants for accepting payment cards according to EuroCommerce, which represents retail, wholesale and international trade in the Union.

HOFFMAN ESTATES, Illinois - Sears, Roebuck and Co says it will open "home environment" departments in 300 stores this year to tap consumer demand for security systems and air and water treatment products.
SEATTLE, Washington - Starbucks Corp says it will raise coffee prices for the second time this year to reflect skyrocketing prices for the commodity on world markets.

SYDNEY - Older, health-conscious soft drink lovers are driving a A$385 ($295) million "adult-rated" soft drink market in Australia which has taken the industry by surprise, according to research group Mintel Australia. The market makes up 35 percent of Australia's A$1.1 billion non-cola soft drink market.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

CHICAGO - The U.S. food industry is cooking up new products -- with an emphasis on fresh, not frozen foods -- to meet the demands of consumers who want to eat at home but do not have a lot of time to cook. Fresh, vacuum-packaged foods, expanded offerings in supermarket deli departments and ingredients for dishes that can be prepared quickly, are demanded by harried consumers.

SINGAPORE - Southeast Asian art buyers are beginning to set their sights beyond regional shores and eye the Western art market as rising prosperity dissolves geographic and cultural boundaries. Although gallery owners and auction houses still describe the level of buying of Western paintings as a trickle rather than a flood, they are upbeat about the prospects for this market given its growth in recent years.

VATICAN CITY - Electronic fertility predictors that help women assess whether they can have sex without a high risk of pregnancy are ethically acceptable within marriage, the Vatican says. Hi-tech fertility indicator kits allow a woman to assess when she can have sex during her cycle with only minimal risk of getting pregnant, according to their makers.

SINGAPORE - Tamagotch computer pets are so popular that most Singapore schools have banned them from classrooms to keep students focused on their studies. The craze for the egg-shaped virtual reality toy has swept the world since its launch in Japan in early 1996 and has led Taiwan and Hong Kong to ban them in schools.
